passages.text: CERN Open Data terms state that metadata and datasets are provided under CC0 waiver terms.
Other content can have per-item licenses and users should check the license shown on each page.
Content is provided as-is and portal operators do not provide endorsement of downstream analyses.
NanoAOD can be analyzed with common ROOT and Python tools and does not require CMSSW for analysis in this workflow.
Collision NanoAOD workflows must apply validated run or lumisection JSON files linked from the dataset records.
The guide demonstrates both remote root:// access and xrdcp local copy to improve processing stability for larger files.
NanoAOD event data include run and luminosityBlock fields which can be used when applying validated JSON filtering.
The CMS Docker guide provides cmscloud or cms-cloud images for reproducible analysis sessions with mapped ports.
The Python analysis image includes awkward, uproot, and jupyterlab, making it suitable for NanoAOD workflows without CMSSW.
Examples often use latest tags, but reproducible workflows should pin immutable image digests.
cernopendata-client supports deterministic metadata lookup with get-metadata using recid or DOI.
get-file-locations with --protocol xrootd returns file endpoints for streaming access.
download-files supports filter-range so deterministic subsets can be used for bounded demos.
